name: Age Well
description: The Area Agency on Aging for this county: information and assistance, home-delivered and congregate meals, in-home services, transportation, caregiver support and senior legal assistance.
next_step: Call and describe what is hard right now. Ask for information and assistance. The statewide Senior HelpLine, 1-800-642-5119, also reaches your local agency. Military service is not required.
constraints: Many services focus on people age 60 and older and adults with disabilities; eligibility and waitlists vary by program.
In Addison County, Granville and Hancock are served by Central Vermont Council on Aging (802-479-0531).

source_evidence.title: Vermont Department of Disabilities, Aging and Independent Living: Older Americans Act snapshot with Area Agency on Aging map
source_evidence.scope: Each Area Agency on Aging’s service area, with town exceptions, and phone; read in full. The document is dated February 15, 2019, though its title refers to 2023 data. The Department for Children and Families’ Area Agencies on Aging page (https://dcf.vermont.gov/contacts/partners/aaa; read in full, undated) gives the same service areas and the statewide HelpLine, 1-800-642-5119.

name: Vermont Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program (Vermont Legal Aid)
organization: Vermont Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program (Vermont Legal Aid)
description: The regional long-term care ombudsman for this county: advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and residential care facilities.
next_step: Call the regional ombudsman program. Give the facility name and county. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.
Ask for extension 3, the ombudsman. Expect a reply within three business days.

source_evidence.title: Vermont Legal Aid: Vermont Long-Term Care Ombudsman Project
source_evidence.scope: Call 1-800-889-2047 ext. 3 or use the online form; replies within three business days; serves people in licensed long-term care facilities and people getting care at home through Choices for Care; read in full. The program is statewide, so every county shows it.
